title: Jesus, in Thy Dying Woes
description: Jesus, in Thy Dying Woes in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 3 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Thomas Benson Pollock, first published in 1870. The tune, WORDS ON THE CROSS - THE LITANY, is by William Henry Monk (1889). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Je-sus, in Thy dy-ing woes, E-ven while Thy life-blood flows, Cra-ving par-don for Thy foes; Hear us, ho-ly Je-sus.

lines: When our sins Thy pangs renew,
For we know not what we do:
O may we, who mercy need,
Be like Thee in heart and deed,
When with wrong our spirits bleed:

licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
credits: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (openhymnal.org), edited by Brian J. Dumont; public domain.
